entries.title: Sharper ground, tidier phone buttons
items: The ground is much sharper: roads, sand and grass have crisp edges and a fine grain up close instead of a blur.
On phones the skill buttons now sit in two neat rings round Attack, with no overlaps and no keyboard letters. The Next button is gone: tap the monster you want.
Portal swirls now fill their stone rings, and the guide's beam and the portal's name stand on the ring itself.

entries.title: New skills go straight on your bar
items: When you learn a new skill it now goes on your action bar for you, replacing one of the Wanderer's starting skills.
Fighters and Rogues take 10% less damage from every hit.
The King's Road warband packs are one raider smaller.

entries.title: All of Act I is open
items: The rest of the act is here: Highcairn Pass, Redcliff Heights and the Warband Mine (Warlord Ruhk), the Sunken Ruins, Gravewatch Hills, and the Deep Catacomb, three floors down to Harrowmund at the end of the act.
Monsters fit their places better: birds on perches, burrowers at burrows, spiders by egg sacs. Named rares wait where their stories say.
Rogues are tougher (+25% health, +8 dodge), Back Cut from the front now does 75%, and daggers and one-hand swords really do use Agility now.

entries.title: Every specialization is here
items: The last six specializations: Runesmith, Scavenger, Starcaller, Sorcerer, Enchanter and Shade Dancer. All 31 now have three skill trees each.
The Enchanter's sleep holds until something hits the sleeper, and Beguile turns a monster on its own pack until you strike it.
Dusk Priests and Spirit Speakers heal whoever is most hurt by a share of the damage they deal.

Warlocks and Sorcerers pay for their strongest spells in health (never below 30%). The Chronomancer's hastes shorten cooldowns. The Sorcerer's Wild Bolt picks a new element every cast, and the Scavenger's Big Score and Jackpot are true gambles.

entries.title: Elderglade, Mirefen and thirteen more specializations
items: Two new regions: Elderglade, a forest of giant old trees and standing stones, and Mirefen, a marsh of stilt huts and boardwalks. Each has a dungeon beneath it: the Elder Roots, where Ildreth waits, and the Mire Crypt, where Sister Vennel rings her bell.

Thirteen more specializations at level 10: Necromancer, Warlock, Druid, Weaponmaster, Reckoner, Dusk Priest, Bard, Wyrmblood, Tinker, Chronomancer, Spirit Speaker, Hexbreaker and Monk. Druid shapes, Weaponmaster stances, Bard songs and Wyrmblood tempers swap your whole action bar.
Mud and flood water slow everyone who wades through, you and the monsters alike.
Revive skills now bring a fallen friend back, even mid-fight. Skills you have not reached yet are dimmed on your bar.

entries.title: A guide for your first steps, and four new places
items: New heroes get a short welcome in Brightwater, and a gold arrow at your feet now always points to your next step: the right portal in town, the way out of a zone, the stairs down in a dungeon. The quest box says where to go too.
Portals you can use now glow and swirl. Locked ones are dark and say what opens them.
Four new places: Thornwood, the King's Road, Thornwood Hollow (Mother Thrum waits at the bottom) and the Old Barrow (three floors, and Reeve Oswin).
Boss helpers now come out of the room itself: crabs from behind the pillars, rats from the chutes, spiders from the egg sacs, the dead from the coffins.
Mages rest far less: Intellect now adds Mana regen, Mana comes back three times as fast between fights, and Cinder Bolt costs less. Fighters and Rogues are tougher.

entries.title: Skills that do what they say
items: Forked Bolt and Chain Tempest now jump from enemy to enemy. The Assassin's Decoy stands where you drop it. A Knight's oath takes a share of the hits meant for the friend they guard.
Skills that raise your dodge or your speed now really do.
Changing your specialization at the trainer gives back every point you spent and hands you the new one's starting skills.
Smoother on phones: monsters are drawn with fewer pieces.

entries.title: Every monster has its own look, and six more specializations
items: Every monster, rare and boss now has its own model and animations: crabs snap their claws, wasps buzz, Hollowhorn raiders wear their stag paint, ghosts drift and bosses change as they lose health.
Six more specializations at level 10: Knight, Assassin, Frostbinder, Stormcaller, Oracle and Swashbuckler, each with three trees of its own.
Rogues hit harder: Agility now raises dagger and sword damage, Energy comes back faster, and Back Cut lands from the front too (at 60%; full damage from behind).

entries.title: Legendary powers and sharper skills
items: Legendary items now do what they say: each carries a power that reshapes one of your skills (Wide Swing in a full circle, Cinder Bolt leaving fire on the ground, a Long Draw that fires twice, and more).
Back Cut only lands from behind, and Long Draw needs a bow. Breaker Blow pours your whole Temper bar into one hit, so the more you have, the harder it lands.
Poison Coat now coats your weapon for 20 seconds. Sanctify and Thunderhead leave a lasting patch on the ground.
Controllers work in every menu: the d-pad moves a highlight, A presses, B goes back.

entries.title: Specializations and the first dungeons
items: At level 10 choose a specialization with three skill trees of its own. The first six are here: Vanguard, Ranger, Pyromancer, Cleric, and two that bridge Paths, the Paladin (Fighter or Healer) and the Spellblade (Fighter or Mage). Rangers and Pyromancers bring a companion.
The trainer in Brightwater can unlearn your skills or change your specialization, for a price.
The first dungeons are open: the Tidecaves under the Saltgrass headland (two floors, and Clatterjaw waiting in his pool) and the Mill Cellars under the windmill (Gristmaul).
Fixed: armour from skills now protects you, and skills that make enemies hit softer now do.

entries.title: Click to move
items: On a computer you can now play with the mouse: click the ground to walk there (hold the button to keep walking toward the pointer), and click a monster to walk up to it and fight.
Right-click uses the first skill on your bar on whatever is under the pointer. Keys 1-6 fire the rest; a skill that is out of reach walks you into range first.
Clicking a portal, exit, waypoint or townsperson walks you there and uses it. Your hero finds a way round rocks and walls.
WASD still works if you prefer it.

entries.title: Brightwater, the first zones, champions and crafting
items: You now start in Brightwater, a harbour town. Visit the trader, potion seller, gambler, crafter, stash, trainer and the mercenary hall.
The first real zones are open: Saltgrass Shore (levels 1-3) through the town portals, and Windmill Fields (levels 3-5) beyond it. Walk onto a waypoint to remember it; press M for the map.
Press T anywhere for your own recall portal to town. Walk back into it to return to the same spot.

Champions: tougher monsters with a coloured ring and special powers (thorns, burning trails, wards, summoners and more). Each one tells you what it is in its name. Named rares turn up some days and not others.
Crafting shards drop from monsters. Select one in your bag and tap an item to reshape it, or break unwanted items into shards. The crafter can upgrade shards.
Hire a mercenary (shield-bearer, archer or hedge-mage) who levels with you and wears gear you give them.
Trade with friends anywhere: tap their name on the left.
Bosses have phases and an enrage timer; the dungeons that hold them open soon.

entries.title: Paths, loot and a real meadow
items: At level 3 choose your Path: Fighter, Rogue, Mage or Healer. Each has its own skill tree to spend a point in every level, and its own way to fight. Fighters build Temper by hitting and getting hit; Rogues spend Energy that refills fast.
Six skill slots: keys 1-6, the buttons, or the arc on a phone. Press K for your skills; tap the arrow on a skill, then a slot, to put it on your bar.

Monsters drop loot now: gold, potions and gear. Everyone gets their own drops. Good items stand in a beam of light. Click or tap a drop to pick it up (Space picks up the nearest one), and open chests the same way.
Potions refill over a few seconds, and drinking two at once doubles the refill. Q drinks a healing potion, E a mana potion, straight from your belt.
Drag items around your bag and onto your body. Right-click identifies an unidentified item, for free.
Proving Meadow has been rebuilt: a road and a camp, a pond with a dock, a farm, old ruins, woods, a cliff, and four chests to find.
Zoom in and out with the mouse wheel, or pinch on a phone.

entries.title: Monsters, fights and gear
items: The meadow has monsters now: tideling crabs, shoal snappers, gullhawks and more, in packs, patrols and swarms. Each kind fights its own way: brutes close in, archers keep their distance, shamans heal their friends, and leaders run for help when they're losing.
Fight with Attack, Sure Strike, Spark, Field Mend and Shove (keys F and 1-4, or the buttons). Skills share a short global cooldown, and spells have a cast bar that moving cancels.
Watch the ground: a red shape shows where a big attack will land, so step out of it. Shove stops an enemy's spell.
Fall in battle and a friend can bring you back (stand next to you and press R), or return to the waypoint. Your gear wears down a little each time.
Press C for your character: equipment, attribute points to spend every level, and your bag. Right-click an item to identify or equip it.
Every hero starts with a short sword, a linen robe and a rope sash.

entries.title: First steps
items: Rogueloot is open! This is the very first build: walk a meadow as a Wanderer, alone or with up to three friends.
Play solo, host a game and share its code, or join a friend with theirs.
Move with WASD or the arrow keys, a controller's stick, or the thumb stick on a phone. Up is always north.
Coming next: fighting, loot, Paths and the first zones of Act 1.
